findings: 0 of 994 targets are eligible for VERIFIED_REUSE. With the observations the state table is row-for-row the table without them: R2 (static R2S) refuses all 667 targets that pass I6 before impact.py reads any observation (no state carries evidence.observation), and I6 leaves the other 327 UNRESOLVED before any section 2.9 rule.

Expectation confirmed in part: tests/v2/test_p9_reproduction.py's directory constant 'closure-evidence/v2' names all 9 delta files (the 9 closure-evidence/v2 additions since v2.2.0), but it is one of 15 files of S(F) that do; the reason the engine prints is the first in path order (closure-evidence/v2/v2.1/campaign-supp/tools/make_queue.py, a path construction holding 'closure-evidence').

Records: 97 of 97 recorded, 96 PASS and 1 TIMEOUT (tests/v2/test_v21_continue_integrity.py under strace with 4 workers); 41 complete, 56 incomplete. Dominant cause: aliases (55): git's object writes in scratch repositories (link/symlink of relative '.git/...' strings, no directory fd) are resolved against every cwd any task had, the tree included, so each counts as a new name for a tree path (53 records); 2 records from /proc or /dev/fd paths. Other counters: tests_unparsed 19, unparsed_lines 6, tracer_exit 1, cwd_unresolved 1. No record was refused by verify (re-hash and re-derive): 41 OK, 56 with completeness gaps only.

Diagnostics only (test-only rules switched off; no authority): with R2S off, D2 refuses 61 of the 63 linux targets and R0 2 (the entry's interpreter is unproven). Every D2 miss of every record is a path that is a file of neither commit: tree-root names such as '*.py', 'test_*.py', '__init__.py', 'calc.py', 'app/calc.py', and code compiled under synthetic file names ('aisef2/x.py', 'tests/v2/t.py'); 0 records miss a real file outside S(F). With R2S and D2 off: R1 48, R8 13 (first site reported: aisef/__init__.py:1), R0 2. With R2S, D2, R1 and R8 off: 40 would be reused, R0 22 (20 by the TIMEOUT record, 2 interpreter unproven), R3 1. Those 40 are not eligible: four refusing rules had to be switched off to reach them.

A full observation of all 262 kill files would change no count: the 327 stop at I6 and the 667 at R2S, both before impact.py consults an observation, as long as the 9 delta files remain and S(F) names them (the two S(F) whose namers were computed hold 15 each; all 97 S(F) have the same 7544 files). Even with R2S off, the 604 non-linux targets that pass I6 stay R0 (no observation of their kill files 367 here, measured on darwin 115, flavor unproven 122) unless observed on their own flavor; the darwin ones would need the audit backend. Argued from the rule order in impact.py rules(); not run.
judging: impact.py --classify ran on the observing host in a separate full-history clone at the same commit (clean, not shallow), not on the darwin host: the 97 witnesses total 3.97 GB and bringing them to the darwin host would have left it below the 20 GiB free-disk floor. The no-observation table computed on the darwin host (CPython 3.14.7) and on the observing host (CPython 3.12.3) are byte-identical (classification.without_observations_*).
